canonical_title: Ecological State at a Temporal Cut: Sparse Semantic Access
state_concept: the present is a zero-duration observational cut; ecological state is the least quotient induced on that cut by retrospective, transverse latent-present, and prospective distinguishability/access constraints
headline: retrospective-transverse-prospective cut geometry and sparse prospective access determine the induced ecological state quotient
headline_quantity: state quotients are computed from pre-state semantic classes, prospective access relations, legal traces, and induced equivalence on the temporal cut
theory_contribution: characterize ecological state as the unique coarsest quotient preserving the cut observation and declared pre-state signatures; prove representation invariance, identify the fixed-cut state space with the partition-refinement interval, and characterize deterministic transport between cuts by quotient descent; then specialize retrospective carried semantics, transverse candidate-safe latent response structure, and prospective query accessibility to quantify sparse prospective access
novelty_boundary: CREST does not claim novelty for quotient state abstraction, Mobius/Harsanyi accounting, unanimity games, or finite counting once the access relation is fixed. The contribution is the finite temporal-boundary theory, strict companion realizability boundaries, pre-state retrospective/transverse/prospective structure, and explicit separation of prerequisite order from sparse prospective coverage. The manuscript does not claim a proved continuous-time epsilon-to-zero or germ limit theorem.

temporal_boundary_geometry.present: zero-duration observational cut represented at one indexed time, not a finite observation interval
temporal_boundary_geometry.retrospective: MLTR carried semantics arriving from the left of the cut
temporal_boundary_geometry.transverse: MRM candidate-safe latent response structure within a visible-cut fiber; not complete ontic mechanism identity
temporal_boundary_geometry.state: least cut quotient compatible with retained retrospective, transverse, and prospective distinctions
temporal_boundary_geometry.continuous_time_boundary: finite idealization only; no shrinking-window epsilon-to-zero or continuous-time germ theorem is claimed

realizability_boundaries.fixed_partition_bound: fixed precomputed partitions on a one-class baseline cannot generate positive interaction by common refinement alone
realizability_boundaries.immutable_history_no_activation: a zero-debt post-cut audit preserving raw MLTR history cannot become nontrivial by rewriting the past
realizability_boundaries.fixed_grammar_mrm_zero_debt: candidate-safe zero debt under one fixed grammar implies a singleton MRM response type

semantic_companions.history: CREST consumes complete MLTR carried maps and quotients raw routes by equality of carried semantics; this is the retrospective left-of-cut structure
semantic_companions.latent_response: CREST quotients primitive MRM candidate laws by equality of complete declared response tables; this is transverse latent-present structure inside a visible-cut fiber rather than full mechanism identity
semantic_companions.future: CCOC prospective responsibility is a declared legal right-of-cut query grammar

sparse_semantic_access.interpretation: prerequisite structure fixes the interaction order; prospective semantic coverage changes its magnitude

canonical_numeric_witness.claim_boundary: finite semantic-access witness, not an empirical ecological constant

complete_access_boundary.status: v0.6 full-addressability boundary case, not canonical v0.7 witness

shallow_lake_prerequisite_audit.status: worked ecological interpretation with an executable literature-grounded finite model; not empirical validation and not a state-design prescription
shallow_lake_prerequisite_audit.composed_target_form: binary history-response concordance versus mismatch diagnostic
shallow_lake_prerequisite_audit.validation: minimum prerequisite sets are computed by target factorization and counterfactual interface substitution; the binary composed target has both outputs within every fixed-H and every fixed-Theta slice
shallow_lake_prerequisite_audit.literature_boundary: Sondergaard et al. 2003, Sondergaard et al. 2007, and Jeppesen et al. 2012 support sediment-P legacy, biological inertia, and multiple restoration channels; they do not assert the exact parity diagnostic used as the minimal finite joint-dependence witness

literature_positioning.hysteresis_and_state_shifts: Scheffer et al. 2001; Beisner, Haydon, and Cuddington 2003
literature_positioning.bisimulation_and_state_abstraction: Givan, Dean, and Greig 2003; Li, Walsh, and Littman 2006

supporting_results: v0.6 complete addressability is the k=N boundary of the sparse semantic-access model
abstract fixed-closure marked-cycle Delta=log2(n)-1 remains an exact supporting extremum but not a literal immutable-history theorem
abstract fixed-closure b-log2(3) three-audit family remains a supporting extremum rather than the companion-derived headline
six-world obstruction-change diagnostics remain compatibility regressions

representation_invariance.criterion: two signature families induce the same cut state iff each family mutually factors through the state induced by the other
representation_invariance.redundancy_corollary: adding signatures already determined by the induced state leaves the quotient unchanged
representation_invariance.interpretation: the generated equivalence relation, not signature names or coordinate encoding, determines the cut state

cut_state_space.carrier: representation-equivalence classes of finite pre-state signature families
cut_state_space.canonical_image: all partitions refining the visible cut partition B_t
cut_state_space.order: more information corresponds exactly to partition refinement
cut_state_space.realizability: every refinement of B_t is realizable by one signature whose kernel is that refinement
cut_state_space.complexity_monotonicity: adding signatures can only refine the state, so log2(number of quotient classes) is nondecreasing

temporal_cut_transport.criterion: a deterministic world map descends iff source-equivalent worlds always map to target-equivalent worlds
temporal_cut_transport.uniqueness: the induced quotient transition is unique whenever it exists
temporal_cut_transport.composition: identity and composition descend for compatible finite world evolutions
temporal_cut_transport.obstruction: failure means one source state class reaches multiple target state classes
temporal_cut_transport.scope: no stochastic or multivalued transport theorem, no temporal monotonicity of state cardinality, and no continuous-time limit
